title: Local-ring identifications with w-local target
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings identifying every local ring: for every prime $q\subset B$, the induced map $A_{q\cap A}\to B_q$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. If $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is w-local [def-weil-pbc-w-local], then $B$ is ind-Zariski over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], that is, a filtered colimit of finite products of principal localizations $A_f$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away].

proof.text: For a finitely presented A-algebra P mapping to B and a prime q of B, invert the given A-algebra isomorphism A_p ≃ B_q, where p is the contraction. Apply Algebra.factors_through_principal_localization to descend P → A_p to a map β : P → A_f for f outside p. Localization extensionality identifies the composite P → A_f → B_q with the original map.

Set g₀ to the image of f in B and map A_f canonically to B_g₀. Choose a finite polynomial presentation t of P. For each generator the difference between the two maps into B_g₀ vanishes in B_q. Write that difference with denominator a power of g₀; the numerator is annihilated by some b_i outside q. Put g = g₀ times the product of the b_i. Mapping the annihilator identities to B_g and cancelling the now-invertible b_i proves equality on generators. Polynomial extensionality and surjectivity of t give P → A_f → B_g factoring the localized original map.

Use the proved upstream WLocalSpace.closedPointsHomeomorph from the w-local API: the closed points are homeomorphic to the connected components. They are compact Hausdorff and totally disconnected. Mathlib TopologicalSpace.IsOpenCover.exists_finite_nonempty_disjoint_clopen_cover refines the D(g) cover on closed points. Pull its finite partition back along the continuous map H.symm ∘ ConnectedComponents.mk. If x specializes to a closed c, Specializes.connectedComponents_mk_eq shows this map sends x to c. Thus openness ensures the pulled-back part stays in its selected D(g). Empty spectra and empty partitions are included.

Choose idempotents e_i representing the clopen partition. PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen_injOn_isIdempotentElem and basicOpen_mul turn disjointness into e_i e_j = 0. OrthogonalIdempotents.isIdempotentElem_sum makes their sum idempotent. At any prime, one e_i is outside the prime; multiplying a supposed membership of the sum by this e_i contradicts orthogonality. Hence the sum has the same basic open as 1 and equals 1 by idempotent injectivity. Apply Mathlib CompleteOrthogonalIdempotents.bijective_pi to identify B with the product of B/(1-e_i).

The image of g_i is a unit in B/(1-e_i): if its principal ideal were proper, Ideal.exists_le_maximal would give a maximal ideal containing it. Its contraction to B avoids e_i, since it contains 1-e_i and is proper, contradicting D(e_i) ⊆ D(g_i). Extend B → B/(1-e_i) to B_gᵢ by localization. Compose each A_fᵢ → B_gᵢ with that extension, take the product and then the inverse Chinese remainder isomorphism. The selected local factorization equations give P → ∏ A_fᵢ → B with the required composite.

Use the Mathlib instances IsLocalization.Away.finitePresentation and Algebra.FinitePresentation.pi, then Algebra.FinitePresentation.equiv, to see that every A-algebra equivalent to a finite product of A_f is finitely presented. This is a one-line instance inference and transport in Lean; it includes the empty product and needs no étaleness theorem.

Let E be the set of A-algebras equivalent to finite products of principal localizations. The preceding factorization applies to every finitely presented algebra mapping to B. Apply CommAlgCat.exists_filtered_colimit_of_factorization to E. Package its small filtered diagram, cocone and IsColimit proof as a ColimitPresentation. Membership of every term in E is exactly the term condition in IsIndPrincipalZariski A B.
